item.title: Kyoto at New Year: Okera-mairi, Temple Bells & a Day-by-Day Plan
item.description: Kyoto at New Year does something no other Japanese city manages: it keeps its temples and gardens open while the rest of the country shuts, and it adds rituals that have been performed on these exact streets for a thousand years. On the night of December 31, people queue at Yasaka Shrine to catch a sacred flame on a length of braided rope, then walk it home through the dark to light the first soup of the year.
